AUTHOR: M. C. Fiorentino; A. Mancini; F. D. Nardo; A. D. Anno; E. Fanelli; I. Martino; M. Anzani; G. Russo; C. H. Friederichs; D. Scaradozzi
TITLE: Deep Learning-Based Fish Detection in Challenging ROV Images: a YOLOv8 Approach for Offshore Environmental Monitoring
VENUE: 2026 34th Mediterranean Conference on Control and Automation (MED)
REGION: Mediterranean Sea (Italy), around offshore oil/gas platforms
DATA: Own/partner (ENI) ROV images, ~2,600 images from 9 platform subsets merged into 6 composite datasets
V_EV: Sec III-A/Table I: 'operational depths (2-72 m), resulting in substantial variability in water color, visibility, and ambient illumination across subsets'
D2: 5-fold CV (80/20) within each of six composite datasets
D_EV: Sec III-A: 'Each composite dataset was partitioned into five equal folds ... corresponding to an 80/20 train-test split per fold.'
R_EV: Sec III-A: training and test folds drawn from the same platform datasets; no external evaluation
C_EV: Sec III-E: 'computed at a confidence threshold of 0.6 and an IoU threshold of 0.5.'
E_EV: Table III: only 'Precision, Recall, F1, mAP50' (and CO2) reported
METR: Precision, recall, F1, mAP50, training time, CO2
NOTE: Folds are image-level partitions within composite (per-platform) datasets; not split by platform. Depth per platform reported (Table I); visibility/illumination only qualitative, no stratified results. Confidence threshold 0.6 unexplained -> C_ALL N. Habitat = artificial offshore structures (ENV NR). Image count stated as ~2,600 though Table I image column sums lower (table scrambled).
